title: Malayalam

how.d: Short, plain-English explanations — no grammar walls, no jargon without a translation.
Each phrase speaks in a native Malayalam voice. Slow it to 0.2× and repeat until it sticks.
Every topic ends in practice: quiz yourself, then review the words until they stay.

hfaqs.a: No. Start with spoken Malayalam in Roman letters, and let the script come second. Learners who speak first stay motivated far longer than learners who drill letters for a month before saying a word.
hfaqs.q: Must I learn the Malayalam script before speaking?

hfaqs.a: നമസ്കാരം for respect, അതെ and ഇല്ല, നന്ദി, ദയവായി, ശരി, and ഞാൻ — I. With those seven you can open any interaction in Kerala politely while your vocabulary grows underneath.
hfaqs.q: Which words should I learn in week one?

hfaqs.a: The famous ഴ plus retroflexes — ള, ണ, long-short vowel pairs. Ten minutes of daily listening retunes your ears within weeks; the pronunciation page walks you through each one.
hfaqs.q: What is the hardest part of Malayalam?

topics.desc: നമസ്കാരം opens every door in Kerala — plus mornings, welcomes and warm goodbyes. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Yes, and nobody will mind — നമസ്കാരം with folded hands is understood and loved everywhere Malayalam is spoken. With close friends a smile and സുഖമാണോ? (are you well?) feels warmer.
faqs.q: Can I just say namaskaram everywhere?

faqs.a: നമസ്കാരം with folded hands and a small nod, and നിങ്ങൾ (ningal — formal you) until invited closer. Add ചേട്ടൻ (chettan) or ചേച്ചി (chechi) for someone slightly older — it warms everything instantly.
faqs.q: How do I greet an elder respectfully?

faqs.a: വീണ്ടും കാണാം (veendum kaanaam — we'll meet again) is the warm standard. പോയിട്ട് വരാം (poyitt varaam — I'll go and come back) is the classic respectful farewell — receive it with a smile and a nod.

topics.note: A note on സുഖമാണോ vs സുഖമല്ലേ. സുഖമാണോ? (sughamaano) is the everyday are you well? — warm, quick, everywhere. സുഖമല്ലേ? is its cosy confirmation-style twin, heard among friends. Start with സുഖമാണോ; the rest arrives with ammamas.
paras: നമസ്കാരം (namaskaram) is the one greeting that never fails. Folded hands, a small nod, and it works with strangers, elders, shopkeepers and officials — exactly the people a learner meets first. Say it clearly, hold the folded hands half a second, and Kerala opens to you.

Mornings get their own greeting: സുപ്രഭാതം (suprabhaatam — good morning), heard in offices, schools and chayakadas until about eleven. Evenings soften to ശുഭസായാഹ്നം (shubhasaayaahnam). Time-stamped greetings signal that you live in the language, not just visit it.

Welcomes are grand in Malayali culture: സ്വാഗതം (svaagatam — welcome) opens homes, shops and hearts. Guests are greeted standing, often with water or chaya before a single question. Return the warmth — വന്നു, നന്ദി (I've come, thank you) — and you are family within minutes.

Goodbyes promise return, never end: വീണ്ടും കാണാം (we'll meet again) is the everyday farewell; സൂക്ഷിക്കണം (sookshikkanam — take care) adds affection. Leave every conversation with a നമസ്കാരം and a smile — in Kerala, how you leave is remembered longer than how you came.

topics.desc: Vowels, consonants, conjuncts and the famous ഴ — the Malayalam alphabet without tears. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Fifteen vowels (സ്വരങ്ങൾ) and thirty-six consonants (വ്യഞ്ജനങ്ങൾ) — 51+ letters that combine into conjuncts. Sounds huge, behaves simply: learn the shapes and the combinations assemble themselves.
faqs.q: How many letters does Malayalam have?

faqs.a: ഴ (zha) — the retroflex approximant Malayalam shares with Tamil: പഴം, വാഴ. Curl the tongue back without touching, voice it. Listen, curl, practise: it arrives within weeks.
faqs.q: What is the hardest Malayalam letter?

faqs.a: Yes — in writing: ഖ ഘ ഛ ഝ ഠ ഢ ഥ ധ ഫ ഭ appear in Sanskrit loans (ക്ഷമ, ധർമ്മം). Daily Malayalam softens most of them; recognise them in print, relax in speech.
faqs.q: Does Malayalam have kh, gh, bh sounds?

topics.note: A note on ചന്ദ്രക്കല (chandrakkala). The little crescent ് kills a consonant's hidden vowel: ക is ka, ക് is just k. Malayalam writes pure consonants with the chandrakkala and syllables without — ക് + അ = ക. One crescent, and the whole reading system clicks.
paras: Malayalam vowels (സ്വരങ്ങൾ) come in fifteen: അ ആ ഇ ഈ ഉ ഊ ഋ എ ഏ ഐ ഒ ഓ ഔ അം അഃ. Short and long pairs — അ/ആ, ഇ/ഈ, ഉ/ഊ — change meaning completely: കല (kala — art) versus കാലം (kaalam — time). Length is meaning in Malayalam; stretch with care.

Consonants (വ്യഞ്ജനങ്ങൾ) run five rows deep: ക ഖ ഗ ഘ ങ, ച ഛ ജ ഝ ഞ, ട ഠ ഡ ഢ ണ, ത ഥ ദ ധ ന, പ ഫ ബ ഭ മ — plus യ ര ല വ ശ ഷ സ ഹ ള ഴ റ. Round, curly, generous — the script that writes Tamil's sister with Sanskrit's wardrobe.

Vowels and consonants marry into കൂട്ടക്ഷരങ്ങൾ (koottaksharams): ക് + അ = ക (ka), ക് + ആ = കാ (kaa). Learn the vowel-signs once and every consonant sings the same song — the system is vast but perfectly regular.

Then the crown jewel: ഴ (zha), the retroflex approximant — പഴം (fruit), വാഴ (plantain). Curl the tongue back without touching the roof, voice it, and feel the most Malayali sound in existence. Natives will grin when you land it; the grin is worth weeks of practice.

topics.desc: ഒന്ന് രണ്ട് മൂന്ന് to നൂറ് — plus clock time and market-ready counting. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: International digits for daily life — prices, phones, buses all use them. Malayalam has traditional number words in full use (ഒന്ന്, പത്ത്, നൂറ്) but modern digits in print.
Take the number, add മണി (mani — hour): മൂന്ന് മണി (three o'clock). Half past adds -അര: മൂന്നര is half past three. One rule, every clock in Kerala.
faqs.q: How do I say the time in Malayalam?

faqs.a: എത്ര? (ethra — how much?). Then listen for the number plus രൂപ (roopa — rupees). Market Malayalam is the fastest teacher there is.
faqs.q: How do I ask the price?

topics.note: A note on ഒന്നര, രണ്ടര. Half hours glue -അര to the number: ഒന്നര (1:30), മൂന്നര (3:30), അഞ്ചര (5:30). Every language hides one clock trick; Malayalam's is അര. Learn it and sound native instantly.
paras: One to ten: ഒന്ന് (onn), രണ്ട് (rand), മൂന്ന് (moonn), നാല് (naal), അഞ്ച് (anch), ആറ് (aar), ഏഴ് (ezh), എട്ട് (ett), ഒമ്പത് (ombath), പത്ത് (pathth). Chant them in rhythm — Malayalam numbers love rhythm — and they stick in days, not weeks.

Eleven to nineteen build on പത്ത്: പതിനൊന്ന് (11), പന്ത്രണ്ട് (12), പതിമൂന്ന് (13)... then the tens march: ഇരുപത് (20), മുപ്പത് (30), നാല്പത് (40), അമ്പത് (50), അറുപത് (60), എഴുപത് (70), എൺപത് (80), തൊണ്ണൂറ് (90), നൂറ് (100). Past twenty, glue tens to units — ഇരുപത്തൊന്ന് (21) — and count to a thousand (ആയിരം) without fear.

Money runs on numbers: the currency is the രൂപ (roopa — rupee), and എത്ര? (ethra — how much?) is the most useful sentence in Kerala. Listen for the number, repeat it back — അമ്പത്? (fifty?) — and your first Malayalam transaction completes itself.

Time reuses numbers with മണി (mani — hour): രണ്ട് മണി (two o'clock), അഞ്ച് മണി (five o'clock). ഇപ്പോൾ സമയം എത്ര? (what time is it now?) is the question; half hours add -അര. Numbers, money, clocks: one skill, three daily victories.

topics.desc: Names, homes and small talk — your first real Malayalam conversations, line by line. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: നിങ്ങളുടെ പേര് എന്താണ്? (ningalude perenthaan — what is your name?) for respect; നിന്റെ പേര് എന്താണ്? (ninte perenthaan) for friends and children. Answer with എന്റെ പേര്... (ente per — my name is...). Names first, always.
faqs.q: How do I ask someone's name?

faqs.a: നിങ്ങൾ എവിടെ നിന്ന് വരുന്നു? (where are you from?) — then answer for yourself: ഞാൻ ... നിന്ന് വരുന്നു. Origin questions are the universal second question; prepare your answer before you need it.
faqs.q: How do I say where I'm from?

faqs.a: പതുക്കെ സംസാരിക്കൂ (please speak slowly) and വീണ്ടും പറയൂ (please say it again). Said with a smile, these two sentences make every Malayali slow down and help.
faqs.q: What do I say when people speak too fast?

topics.note: A note on നിങ്ങൾ, നീ and താൻ. Malayalam has two yous where English has one: നിങ്ങൾ (ningal — formal/plural) and നീ (nee — familiar). Start with നിങ്ങൾ for every adult; let friendship invite you to നീ.
paras: Every first conversation follows the same dance: നമസ്കാരം, നിങ്ങളുടെ പേര് എന്താണ്? (what is your name?), എന്റെ പേര്... (my name is...), നിങ്ങൾ എവിടെ നിന്ന് വരുന്നു? (where are you from?). Four lines, and you have had a real conversation. Practise them in order until they flow without thinking.

Small talk runs on three questions: നിങ്ങൾ എന്ത് ചെയ്യുന്നു? (what do you do?), മലയാളം സംസാരിക്കുമോ? (do you speak Malayalam?), ഭക്ഷണം കഴിച്ചോ? (have you eaten? — asked with genuine care). Answer briefly, ask back immediately — നിങ്ങൾ? — because conversations are volleys, not speeches.

When the torrent comes — and Malayali hospitality pours words — deploy the brakes: പതുക്കെ സംസാരിക്കൂ (please speak slowly), എനിക്ക് മനസ്സിലായില്ല (I didn't understand), വീണ്ടും പറയൂ (please say it again). Every Malayali honours these instantly; they are the learner's seatbelt.

Close warmly and promise return: നിങ്ങളെ കണ്ടതിൽ സന്തോഷം (pleased to meet you), വീണ്ടും കാണാം (we'll meet again). Leave with a നമസ്കാരം and the door stays open — Malayalam conversations end the way they begin: with folded hands.

topics.desc: പോകുക, വരിക, കഴിക്കുക — the twelve verbs that run daily life, plus how they bend. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Malayalam verbs are cited in -ഉക form: പോകുക (to go), വരിക (to come). Polite commands end in -ൂ: പോകൂ (please go), വരൂ (please come). Learn citation forms first, politeness second.
ഞാൻ പോകുന്നു (I go), നീ പോകുന്നു (you go), അവൻ പോകുന്നു (he goes) — same form! Malayalam verbs don't change by person, only by tense. The easiest verb system in India.
ഇല്ല (illa — no/not) negates everything simply: അറിയില്ല (don't know), വേണ്ട (don't want). One negator, endless uses — Malayalam keeps no simple.
faqs.q: How do I say no to a verb?

topics.note: A note on വരൂ vs വാ. വാ (vaa) calls a friend to come; വരൂ (varoo) welcomes a guest like royalty. Same verb, different universe — the -ൂ ending is pure respect. When in doubt, add the respect: Malayalis forgive stiff politeness instantly and casual rudeness never.
paras: Twelve verbs carry daily life: പോകുക (go), വരിക (come), കഴിക്കുക (eat), കുടിക്കുക (drink), വായിക്കുക (read), എഴുതുക (write), ചെയ്യുക (do), സംസാരിക്കുക (speak), കൊടുക്കുക (give), എടുക്കുക (take), ഇരിക്കുക (sit/stay), നോക്കുക (see). Memorise these and you can order food, find toilets, make friends and survive beautifully.

The miracle: verbs don't conjugate by person. ഞാൻ പോകുന്നു (I go), നീ പോകുന്നു (you go), അവൻ പോകുന്നു (he goes), അവർ പോകുന്നു (they go) — one form fits all. Learn tense once, use it for everyone: പോയി (went), പോകും (will go).

Polite commands end in -ൂ: പോകൂ (please go), വരൂ (please come), കഴിക്കൂ (please eat), പറയൂ (please say). This one ending turns every order into an invitation — it is the most useful suffix in Malayalam, worth more than a hundred nouns.

Existence closes the kit: ഉണ്ട് (und — it is / there is) anchors locations — പുസ്തകം മേശമേൽ ഉണ്ട് (the book is on the table). ഇല്ല (illa — there isn't) removes — പണം ഇല്ല (no money). Twelve verbs plus ഉണ്ട്/ഇല്ല: the engine room of Malayalam.
